claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is SUPERSEDED.
In CodePipeline SUPERSEDED execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In CodePipeline SUPERSEDED mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts, so a queued execution behind a busy CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` can be superseded and never run.
Setting CodePipeline execution mode to QUEUED makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn.
CodePipeline QUEUED execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (pipelineType V2).
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands allow setting `executionMode` and `pipelineType`.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that prevents concurrent runs of a deployment job targeting that environment.
An Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the exclusive lock check applies to the stage referencing the environment.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older queued runs waiting behind it are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, one at a time, in order.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
Link targets exist: /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ and /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` and `args: --yes`.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
In TeamCity, the build configuration advanced option "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" is located under the configuration's General Settings.
In TeamCity, the default value of "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" is 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 queues a second build behind the first, running it only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
A cross-reference to the update conflicts troubleshooting page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists.
In Azure Pipelines, serializing Pulumi deployments is done by adding an exclusive lock check to the environment the deployment job targets, with `lockBehavior: sequential` set on the stage.
`lockBehavior: sequential` is a valid Azure Pipelines stage-level setting that queues runs against a resource with an exclusive lock check.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
Setting an AWS CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
In AWS CodePipeline, the default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes deployments.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
